note: Written for this app from each verse's own meaning, as a suggestion for daily life. Not from the book and not a paraphrase of its commentary; shown in the app marked as such.

days.1: The blind king asks what "my sons and the sons of Pandu" did, already dividing mine from theirs. Notice today when you sort people into mine and not mine, at work, at home or in the news, and how quickly it colours what you see.
days.2: Even the greatest archer sank down when the task in front of him felt unbearable. If you feel overwhelmed today, don't pretend you aren't. Arjuna's honesty about his collapse is what opened the door to the teaching.
days.3: Arjuna stops arguing and says: I am confused, teach me. Asking for guidance is not weakness. Today, bring one real confusion to someone wiser, or to this practice, and listen without defending your position.
days.4: Krishna's first words gently question Arjuna's grief. When sorrow or worry arrives today, pause and ask whether it is about what is truly lost or about your fear. Feel it fully, but don't let it decide for you.
days.5: You existed before this morning's worries and you will outlast them. When a day feels like everything, remember the part of you that was there before it began and is untouched by how it goes.
days.6: You have already been a child, a teenager and a younger adult, and something in you stayed the same through all of it. Look at an old photo today if you can, and notice the one who is still here.
days.7: Heat and cold, praise and criticism, good news and bad all come and go. When something pleasant or unpleasant happens today, quietly tell yourself that this too comes and goes, and keep doing what is in front of you.
days.8: What keeps changing cannot be your deepest support. Notice what you lean on for your sense of worth today, a role, a number or someone's approval, and remember that what is real in you does not rise and fall with it.
days.9: What you truly are was never born and will never die. When fear of loss or of growing older grips you today, take one slow breath and remember that it touches the body and the mind, not the Self.
days.10: We change clothes without grieving for the old ones. As you get dressed today, let it remind you that bodies, roles and stages of life are coverings, and the wearer remains.
days.11: No insult, failure or loss can cut, burn, wet or dry the Self. If something stings today, notice that the hurt lands on the mind and on your image of yourself, not on who you are.
days.12: Give your full effort to today's work and loosen your grip on the result. Before one important task today, decide to do it as well as you can, then let the outcome be what it will be.
days.13: Evenness of mind is itself Yoga. When something goes well or badly today, try to meet both the same way: a quiet acknowledgement, then back to the next thing that needs doing.
days.14: Acting well without being bound by the action is a skill, and it can be practised. Choose one ordinary task today, a meal, a message or a conversation, and give it complete attention as an offering rather than a means to an end.
days.15: The steady person is content within, not dependent on getting what they want. Notice one desire that pulls at you today and see if you can let it pass, resting for a moment in contentment just as you are.
days.16: A tortoise draws in its limbs when it needs to. Choose a time today to draw in your senses: put the phone away, close the screens, and sit for a few minutes without taking anything in.
days.17: Dwelling on something leads to attachment, then desire, then anger, then confusion. Catch the first step today: when you notice yourself replaying something you crave or resent, gently turn your attention elsewhere.
days.18: The ocean stays full and still while rivers pour into it. Let wants, news and demands flow into you today without being shaken by each one. You can receive them without needing to act on all of them.
days.19: Arjuna asks why he must act if understanding is higher. Confusion about what to do is normal. If you feel torn between choices today, write down clearly what is actually being asked of you before you decide.
days.20: Work done only for oneself binds; work done as an offering frees. Choose one task today and offer it inwardly before you begin, to God or to the good of others, and notice how it changes the way you work.
days.21: Do what needs doing without clinging to it. Today, finish one duty you have been putting off, simply because it is yours to do, not for credit or reward.
days.22: People follow what we do more than what we say. Someone is watching how you speak, work and react today, perhaps a child, a colleague or a friend. Let your actions be worth copying.
days.23: Nature does the work while the ego claims the credit and the blame. When you succeed or fail today, remember how many things beyond you made it happen, and hold both lightly.
days.24: Your own path, walked imperfectly, is better than someone else's walked well. Notice today when you compare your life with another's, then return to what is truly yours to do and do it wholeheartedly.
days.25: Desire and anger are named as the real enemy. When anger rises today, ask what you wanted that you did not get. Seeing the desire underneath often loosens the anger's grip.
days.26: Whenever Dharma declines, the Lord comes forth. When the world feels dark today, remember that goodness is never abandoned, and look for one small way to stand on the side of Dharma yourself.
days.27: The Lord comes to protect the good and set things right. Protect something good in your own corner of the world today: a person treated unfairly, a promise you made, a habit that keeps you steady.
days.28: The wise find stillness inside activity and activity inside stillness. In the busiest moment of your day, look for the quiet witness within you that is not rushed at all.
days.29: This verse is often chanted before meals. Before you eat today, pause and see the food, the eating and the one who eats as held in the Divine, and let one meal become an offering.
days.30: Knowledge comes to those who approach with humility, sincere questions and service. Today, ask one genuine question of someone who knows more than you, and really listen to the answer.
days.31: Nothing purifies like true understanding, and it comes in its own time. If progress feels slow, keep your daily practice anyway. Understanding grows quietly, like one verse a day.
days.32: Giving up action and acting rightly both lead to freedom, but acting rightly is the easier road. You do not need to escape your responsibilities to grow. Let your ordinary duties be your practice today.
days.33: A lotus leaf rests on water but stays dry. Take part fully today in a situation that usually upsets you, a tense meeting or a hard conversation, while letting its stress roll off you.
days.34: The wise see the same Self in a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcast. Notice whom you treat as less important today, a server, a stranger, an animal, and offer them the same respect.
days.35: Knowing the Lord as the friend of all beings brings peace. When you feel alone or unsupported today, remember that you are not outside that friendship, and neither is anyone you meet.
days.36: Renunciation is not giving up activity but doing what must be done without depending on the result. Notice today the difference between doing a task and needing it to turn out a certain way.
days.37: You are your own friend and your own enemy. Notice how you talk to yourself after a mistake today, and speak to yourself as a good friend would: honestly, but in a way that lifts you up.
days.38: Practice grows on moderate food, sleep, work and rest. Look at one of these today. Is there a small change, an earlier night or a lighter dinner, that would make your mind steadier?
days.39: A lamp in a windless place does not flicker. Sit somewhere quiet for a few minutes today and let your attention rest on one thing, your breath or a sacred word, steady like that flame.
days.40: The yogi finds the one Self everywhere, and everything resting within that Self. As you pass people today, quietly remember that the same awareness looking out of your eyes looks out of theirs.
days.41: Even Krishna agrees the mind is restless; it is trained by practice and by letting go. Don't wait to feel calm before you practise. Keep one small daily habit, like this one, and release a little of what pulls at you.
days.42: Of all who practise, the one who worships with faith and a heart absorbed in the Lord is dearest. Whatever your practice today, prayer, chanting or study, bring your heart into it, not just your hands and eyes.
days.43: Few people even try to seek the truth. That you are here, studying a verse a day, is already rare. Don't measure yourself against anyone today; just keep showing up.
days.44: Everything is strung on the Lord like pearls on a thread. Look at the different parts of your day, work, family, chores and rest, and remember the one thread running through them all.
days.45: Maya is hard to cross by effort alone; those who take refuge in the Lord cross it. When you feel stuck in a pattern you cannot break today, try a moment of surrender: I can't do this alone, please help me.
days.46: After many lives the wise one sees that Vasudeva is all. Try seeing one difficult person or situation today as part of that same Whole, rather than as something outside it working against you.
days.47: What we remember at the end grows from what we dwell on every day. Notice what fills your mind in spare moments today, in queues or on walks, and gently fill some of them with remembrance of the Lord.
days.48: Remember the Lord at all times, and do your work. Devotion and duty are not rivals. Today, link a repeated action, opening a door or starting the car, with a brief remembrance.
days.49: The Lord is easily reached by one who remembers constantly. Think of remembrance today as many small moments, a Name repeated or a thought turned toward God, rather than one big effort.
days.50: All this is pervaded by the Lord in an unseen form. As you go about today, notice the space between things, the sky and the silence between sounds, and let it remind you of what holds everything.
days.51: To those who worship with undivided devotion, the Lord brings what they lack and keeps what they have. When worry about money, health or the future comes today, do what you can and entrust the rest.
days.52: A leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water, offered with love, is accepted. Offering need not be grand. Today, offer something small with love: a flower at your altar, a glass of water, a kind word.
days.53: Whatever you do, eat, give or practise can be offered. Pick three ordinary moments today, eating, working and helping someone, and quietly offer each one to the Lord.
days.54: The Lord is the same to all; devotion is what brings closeness. Nobody is too ordinary or too far gone. If you feel unworthy today, remember that only the turning of the heart matters.
days.55: Fix your mind on the Lord, be devoted, bow down. Before your day gets busy, take a moment to bow, with your body or inwardly, and give the day to God.
days.56: Everything comes forth from the Lord. When you enjoy something beautiful today, music, a meal or a view, trace it back to its source and let the enjoyment turn into gratitude.
days.57: The Lord is the Self seated in the heart of every being. Before you react to someone today, remember who is seated in their heart too.
days.58: Whatever is glorious or powerful comes from a spark of the Lord's splendour. When you admire a talent today, someone else's or your own, see it as borrowed light, and let that keep both pride and envy away.
days.59: Arjuna asks to see, but only if Krishna thinks him able. When you want something today, try asking with the same humility: let it be given if it is right for me.
days.60: The Lord's splendour is like a thousand suns rising at once. Step outside today, even briefly, and look at the sky or the light. Let it show you how small today's worries are against that vastness.
days.61: Time takes everything in its course. This is meant to clarify, not frighten. Ask yourself today: if my time is limited, what one thing truly matters, and have I given it my attention?
days.62: Be merely the instrument. Approach your work today as an instrument doing its part, not as the one who must control everything. Do your part fully and let the larger outcome rest with God.
days.63: By devotion alone can the Lord be truly known. Study and effort matter, but love opens the door. Let your practice be warm today, not just dutiful.
days.64: Work for the Lord, free from ill will toward any being. Is there someone you hold a grudge against? Take one step toward letting it go today, even if only in your own heart.
days.65: Those who fix their minds on the Lord with faith are the best in Yoga. Faith grows by use. Today, bring one decision or worry to God before you start worrying about it on your own.
days.66: Fix your mind and understanding on the Lord, and you will dwell in Him. When your mind wanders today, don't scold it; bring it gently back, as often as it takes.
days.67: Beyond knowledge and meditation, giving up the fruits of action brings peace. Do one helpful thing today without telling anyone and without expecting thanks.
days.68: The devotee the Lord loves bears no ill will, is friendly and compassionate, free of I and mine, and even in pleasure and pain. Choose one of these qualities today and practise it in a single conversation.
days.69: Those who follow this teaching with faith are dear to the Lord. You have now walked through twelve chapters. Take a moment today to give thanks for the steadiness that brought you this far.
days.70: The body is the field and you are the one who knows it. When you feel tired, hungry or unwell today, notice that you are aware of these states. The knower of the field is not the field.
days.71: Knowledge begins with humility, sincerity and harmlessness. Let one conversation today be free of self-promotion: listen more than you speak, and let someone else have the credit.
days.72: What is to be known has no beginning and cannot be held as an idea, so stop trying to grasp it. Sit quietly for a moment today and simply rest in being aware.
days.73: The Supreme within the body is the witness, the one who permits and supports. Try watching one strong emotion today as a witness would, seeing it rise and fall without being swept along.
days.74: To see truly is to see the Lord equally in all beings, the undying within the dying. Visit, call or think of an elderly or ailing person today, and look past the body to the one within.
days.75: Clarity, restlessness and dullness, the three Gunas, bind everyone. Notice which is strong in you at different hours today, and choose food, company and activity that support clarity.
days.76: The wise see that the Gunas are acting, and know what lies beyond them. When someone irritates you today, see their behaviour as the Gunas at work rather than their true Self, and respond more gently.
days.77: Unswerving devotion carries you beyond the Gunas. On a dull or restless day, don't fight your mood head-on. Turn to devotion, a prayer, a chant, a moment at the altar, and let it lift you.
days.78: The Lord is the ground of immortality and of lasting joy. When you look for happiness in things today, remember the deeper joy they only point toward.
days.79: The world is like a vast tree with its roots above. When you are caught in its branches today, errands, screens and worries, remember the root and give it a few minutes of your attention.
days.80: You are an eternal portion of the Divine. Whatever happened yesterday, your worth is not in question. Begin today with the quiet dignity of knowing where you come from.
days.81: Memory, knowledge and even forgetting come from the Lord in the heart. When you cannot recall something or a solution won't come today, pause, breathe, and turn within before straining harder.
days.82: Whoever knows the Lord as the Supreme worships with their whole being. Today, let your work, your words and your thoughts all lean the same way, toward God.
days.83: Fearlessness, purity of heart, generosity, self-control, truthfulness, gentleness, forgiveness: these are the divine qualities. Choose one today and let it guide a small decision.
days.84: Desire, anger and greed are the three gates to ruin. Before buying, arguing or taking more than you need today, pause at the gate and ask which of the three is speaking.
days.85: Let scripture guide what to do and what to avoid. When unsure today, don't decide by mood or convenience alone. Ask what Dharma, and the teaching you are studying, would counsel.
days.86: A person is made of their faith: as the faith, so the person. Notice today what you truly put your faith in, judging by where your time and attention go, and whether it is worth becoming.
days.87: Speech that is truthful, kind, helpful and causes no distress is an austerity. Before you send a message or speak in a tense moment today, check it against those four.
days.88: Om Tat Sat names the Absolute and sanctifies action. Begin one task today with a quiet Om Tat Sat, and offer whatever comes of it.
days.89: Renunciation lets go of selfish desire; relinquishment lets go of the fruits. You can practise both without leaving home. Today, release one result you have been clinging to.
days.90: Every action rests on five factors: the body, the doer, the instruments, the efforts and the unseen divine. When something does not go your way today, remember you were never the only factor.
days.91: Each person reaches perfection through devotion to their own work. Your job, your household and your studies are not in the way of your spiritual life; done with devotion, they are the way.
days.92: The Lord can be worshipped through one's own work. Before you start work today, dedicate it in a single sentence, then let each task be a flower offered.
days.93: Better your own Dharma done imperfectly than another's done well. If you catch yourself envying someone's path today, return with gratitude to the duties that are truly yours.
days.94: One established in Brahman is serene, neither grieving nor craving, and the same toward all. In one moment of disappointment today, try to stay serene: no grieving over it, no reaching for something else.
days.95: The same Lord lives in every heart and moves every being. When others act in ways you don't understand today, remember the same Lord dwells in them, and be slower to judge.
days.96: Krishna does not command; he asks Arjuna to reflect fully and then choose. Before an important decision today, take time to reflect on what you have learned here, then choose freely and own your choice.
days.97: Krishna promises that the one who fixes their mind on Him will come to Him. Hold on to that promise today, especially if your practice feels weak. It rests on His word, not on your perfection.
days.98: Let go of every other support and take refuge in the Lord alone; do not grieve. Name one burden you have been carrying alone, and consciously place it in God's hands today.
days.99: Arjuna rises: his delusion is gone and he will do as Krishna says. Understanding is meant to become action. Choose one thing you have learned in these hundred days and live it today.
days.100: Where Krishna and Arjuna stand together, guidance and effort side by side, there are fortune, victory and justice. Carry both into your life: keep the Lord close, and keep doing your part. Hari Om.
